headlines.title: Walnut Creek house fire leaves 1 person injured, 2 dogs dead
headlines.description: Fire crews with the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District fought a two-alarm house fire in Walnut Creek on Tuesday afternoon that injured one person and killed two dogs. The call came in at 3:39 p.m. reporting a fire in a single-family residence in the 700 block of Woodwind Place in Walnut Creek, according to Con Fire. Crews arrived to find visible flames and smoke and eventually a second alarm was called on the blaze. The fire was knocked down by 4:30 p.m., but as of 5:30 p.m., firefighters were still at the scene handling hot spots and other issues, Con Fire said. One person was transported to the hospital for smoke inhalation, according to Con Fire, but it is unclear if they were a resident of the home or a neighbor. Two dogs perished in the fire. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

headlines.title: SFMTA announces more Muni service on popular routes
headlines.description: The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency will add more service on key routes starting in a few weeks as more people return to school and work. “These changes will bring immediate improvements to thousands of riders traveling key corridors to school and to work,” SFMTA Director of Transportation Julie Kirschbaum said in a statement, as the agency held its Board of Directors meeting on Tuesday. For students, there will be extra afternoon buses along school routes to help transport them. A stop will be added for the 28R-19th Avenue Rapid bus at Eucalyptus Drive, which SFMTA expects students at Lowell High School to use. “I won’t have to worry about missing the 28 bus and getting to school late anymore because there’s always going to be another one soon,” said Woody Szydlik, a Lowell High School student, in a statement from an SFMTA release. Students and educators traveling from Visitacion Valley to Francisco Middle School will have a direct bus route, eliminating a transfer that was previously required on the 8AX-Bayshore Express bus. SFMTA is also going to increase the frequency of trips for the N-Judah train, which can often get packed during commute hours. Trips will increase from every 10 minutes to every nine minutes during peak hours, a change that could see a 10% increase in space for passengers on the trains, according to Kirschbaum. There will be a higher frequency of buses on the 1-California route, also increasing trips from 10 minutes to nine minutes. Buses on this route in the Presidio and downtown areas should arrive every four to five minutes. The 5R-Fulton Rapid route will have larger buses. Capacity increases will also be made during the busiest times on the 22-Fillmore, 29-Sunset, 38R-Geary Rapid, and 49-Van Ness/Mission. “For the majority of our customers, these changes are not going to make it more complex to navigate the system,” Kirschbaum said at the meeting. “There’s not a lot of learning to do, but we do think customers will see some small but meaningful benefits to their travel.” The changes, Kirschbaum said, are able to happen without additional costs to the agency. SFMTA has identified $250 million in cost savings by reducing redundant service options and adjusting system schedules to boost efficiency. “Our staff is looking at this entire optimization and service puzzle and making smart choices to keep up with our changing conditions,” said Kirschbaum. An overview of the service changes can be found at sfmta.com. The page will be updated Wednesday with more details on the changes.

headlines.title: Man killed in targeted Novato shooting; police search for suspect
headlines.description: A 31-year-old man was killed in what police believe was a targeted, gang-related shooting Tuesday morning, prompting a search for the suspect. Novato police responded to reports of a shooting on Alameda del Prado. Arriving officers found the man suffering from a life-threatening gunshot wound, according to the Novato Police Department. Medics provided emergency care at the scene before transporting him in critical condition to a local hospital, where he later died from his injuries. The suspect fled the scene on foot toward Calle Arboleda before officers arrived. Preliminary investigations indicate the shooting was a targeted attack. Novato police officers, detectives, and crime scene investigators are actively working to locate the suspect and are asking for the community’s assistance. The suspect is described as a Latin man, approximately 5 feet, 6 inches tall. He was last seen fleeing on foot in the area of Calle Arboleda and Alameda del Prado wearing dark pants, a gray hooded sweatshirt, and a black ski mask. Authorities warn the public not to approach the suspect. Anyone who spots him is urged to call 911 immediately. Anyone with information regarding the case or relevant security camera footage is asked to contact the NPD at 415-897-4361 or email crimetips@novato.gov to remain anonymous. Reference case number NP26-2062.

headlines.title: 17th annual Outside Lands festival brings music, food to Golden Gate Park
headlines.description: It’s that time of year again as the 17th annual Outside Lands festival takes over Golden Gate Park for a weekend of music and food. The three-day festival kicks off Friday, featuring 90 bands and an expected attendance of more than 200,000 fans across the weekend. This year’s headlining acts include Doja Cat, Tyler, the Creator, Hozier, Charli XCX, The Strokes, Rufus De La Sol, and PinkPantheress. NBC’s Christie Smith is providing a closer look at what attendees can expect on the festival grounds. While the music is the main draw, the food and drink options are a close second. Festivalgoers will have the option of sampling dishes from 95 Bay Area restaurants, which includes 18 new restaurants this year. The culinary lineup features notable establishments such as Nobu, Brenda’s Soul Food, and the Michelin-starred Angler. Tanya Kollar serves as the food curator for Outside Lands, overseeing the massive operation. In a preview of the festival’s dining experience, Kollar was asked to detail her selection process and explain what makes the food at Outside Lands unique compared to other music festivals. She also weighed in on which two dishes stand out the most this year and offered recommendations on what fans should get to drink.

headlines.title: Gann Fire burns more than 7,000 acres in Calaveras County
headlines.description: Mandatory evacuation orders and warnings remain in effect in Calaveras County as the Gann Fire continues to threaten homes east of Stockton. The wildfire, which started Tuesday evening, has grown to more than 7,000 acres. At least one home has been destroyed by the fire, and while there is no official count of damaged structures, NBC Bay Area crews have observed additional homes destroyed. The growing fire danger in Northern California comes as large wildfires continue burning out of control in Oregon and Washington state. NBC Bay Area’s Kris Sanchez has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Half Moon Bay planning commission to consider zoning changes for housing
headlines.description: Half Moon Bay’s Planning Commission will hold a special meeting Wednesday night to consider zoning changes that supporters say could help pave the way for more housing. Commissioners will review a series of zoning amendments that would allow higher-density development in some areas, expand opportunities for workforce housing and streamline approval for certain affordable housing projects. If approved, the recommendations would move to the City Council for final consideration. The meeting comes weeks after the state of California sued Half Moon Bay and four other cities, alleging they repeatedly failed to complete state-required housing plans. It also follows last month’s City Council approval of a controversial five-story affordable housing project on Kelly Avenue for retired and older local farmworkers. Opponents gathered enough signatures to place that project on the November ballot. Wednesday’s meeting will not determine whether new housing projects are built immediately. The special meeting begins at 7 p.m. at the Ted Adcock Community Center.

headlines.title: Livermore vineyard begins grape harvest earlier than usual
headlines.description: Harvest season is getting an early start at an East Bay vineyard. Las Positas Vineyards in Livermore began harvesting its Verdelho grapes Wednesday, becoming the first vineyard in the area to start picking grapes this year. Winemakers said they typically begin harvesting during the second week of August but decided to start earlier because of this year’s weather. They described it as an unusual growing season, with an early bud break, mild weather and no major heat waves. Las Positas Vineyards’ Verdelho has previously been named the Best White Wine in the San Francisco Chronicle Wine Competition.

headlines.title: San Jose firefighters battle vegetation fire near I-280 on-ramp
headlines.description: San Jose firefighters are responding to a vegetation fire burning near an Interstate 280 on-ramp. The San Jose Fire Department said crews are on the scene in the 0 block of Duane Street, near the I-280 on-ramp from South First Street. At last report, the fire had consumed approximately a half-acre. Fire officials stated that no structures are currently threatened. Authorities are urging the public to avoid the area while firefighters work to contain the blaze.

headlines.title: Preliminary 4.1 magnitude earthquake strikes Mendocino County
headlines.description: A preliminary 4.1 magnitude earthquake struck in Mendocino County, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 5:25 p.m. Tuesday and was centered in Covelo, the USGS said. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: Pedestrian taken to hospital after being hit by driver in San Jose
headlines.description: A pedestrian was taken to a hospital with major injuries Tuesday after they were struck by a driver in San Jose, police said. The collision happened at about 12:05 p.m. in the area of Tully Road and Lucretia Avenue, according to police. The driver stayed at the scene and was cooperative with investigators, police said. Additional information wasn’t immediately available. An investigation is ongoing.

headlines.title: Dallas boy, 10, thanks California lifeguard who rescued him from powerful waves
headlines.description: Back home in Dallas, 10-year-old Nathaniel Rai is still dealing with the aftershock of nearly losing his life on a California beach last month. “I was pretty much on the shore, [and] I got like pulled,” Nathaniel told NBC 5. Nathaniel, who has now seen the viral video of himself being rescued, said he was on a family vacation when their beach day ended with him almost drowning. “I screamed for help,” he said. That call was answered by a 16-year-old lifeguard, Ryder Williams, who said he saw Nathaniel lose his footing. Williams radioed for help as he rushed into the water. “I think one more wave happened and I went unconscious,” Nathaniel said. “When I woke up, Ryder was taking me to shore … I was super thankful because I knew he was going to save my life.” Ryder has been called a hero for saving the boy’s life, but he said he was simply doing the job he loved. Only a few days ago, Nathaniel and his dad got to speak to him to express their gratitude. “I was like, ‘Thank you so much for saving my life and my sister thanked him,'” Nathaniel said. That thank you led to a video chat with both families, according to Nathaniel’s father, Sumit Rai. He said in a serendipitous way, they now feel connected. “It turns out there’s a lot of commonalities between us,” Rai said. “We all really like UFC, so we’re talking about going to a fight together … It also so happens that [Ryder’s father] is a retired firefighter and Ryder wants to follow in his footsteps and be a firefighter. I happen to run a nonprofit for firefighters to screen them for cancer.” It was a scary, tragic situation that revealed that some moments can reveal something bigger. Nathaniel and his dad said they are grateful for it all.

headlines.title: Back to school: Bay Area teachers spend their own money to get supplies they need
headlines.description: As Bay Area teachers prepare for the new school year, many are digging into their own pockets to buy supplies. In the South Bay, most teachers head to a nonprofit called RAFT. It’s a special spot in San Jose with 32,000 square feet of discounted classroom items. “Our educators come here because it’s very, very low cost,” RAFT’s Kate Ball said. “A lot of teachers are sometimes expected to pay out of pocket to supply their classrooms, so we’re trying to help that need.” RAFT said teachers spend between $500 and $1,000 per year on school supplies. At Santee Elementary School in San Jose on Tuesday, Imelda Murillo was getting her classroom ready for her students, who arrive on Monday. “Sometimes we do have donations, like tissue, Kleenex, and things like that, which doesn’t seem like a school would need, but we do,” she said. “Paper towels – sometimes we run out of paper towels – hand soap, disinfectant wipes, those kinds of things that you don’t necessarily think are related to an education, but we need all of those things.” Teachers are given a stipend for the school year. District officials said they wish they could give more. At campuses like Santee, teachers said it’s not nearly enough to cover the costs of giving children the quality education they deserve.
